quantity.name: Ishigami variance and Sobol indices
quantity.observable: First-order and total Sobol indices for the Ishigami function, computed natively by SobolReporter from a Sobol sampler driving a SamplerTransientMultiApp. The published error is the maximum ABSOLUTE first-order index error, which is the declared metric.
quantity.supersedes: The published error field previously carried the variance relative error (0.0608) while the declared tolerance was 0.03 on the absolute Sobol index, so RESULTS.md showed a number that was not the one the verdict was judged on. Raised in review rounds 3, 4 and 5.

reference.source: Ishigami function f=sin(x1)+7 sin^2(x2)+0.1 x3^4 sin(x1), xi~U(-pi,pi)

tolerance.rationale: Declared before sampling; bootstrap confidence intervals are reported with the finite sample estimates.

convergence.batch_mode_note: SamplerTransientMultiApp defaults to mode = normal, which instantiates all 8N sub-applications at once: N=4096 reached 7.5 GB and was killed. mode = batch-restore reuses a small pool and runs N=16384 in minutes. batch-reset is not implemented for this MultiApp type.

availability_correction.previous_claim: The row's limitations field stated 'The deprecated GFunction/SobolStatistics reporter object is unavailable in this MOOSE snapshot' and the indices were reconstructed in Python as a result.
availability_correction.what_is_actually_registered: SobolReporter, SobolStatistics and StatisticsReporter are all registered in this build. Only GFunction is missing. The native path was never blocked; the case routed around an obstacle that was not there.
availability_correction.what_changed: ishigami_native.i now carries a SobolReporter on the StochasticResults vector and emits JSON. The indices are computed inside MOOSE. The Python reconstruction is kept only as an independent cross-check.

monte_carlo_convergence.metric: observed log-log slope of the maximum index error against N; must be at least this steep (more negative)
monte_carlo_convergence.rationale: Plain Monte Carlo Sobol estimates converge as N^-1/2; requiring at least -0.35 allows for finite-sample noise while still demanding the error actually fall.

python_cross_check.metric: relative error of the sample variance over all 8N evaluations against the exact Ishigami variance
python_cross_check.supersedes: Declared earlier the same day as 'maximum absolute difference between the native MOOSE indices and an independent Python reconstruction'. Reconstructing the indices requires knowing the row ordering of the Sobol design in the StochasticResults vector, which is not documented in the artifacts; a reconstruction built on a guessed ordering tests the guess, not MOOSE, and mine disagreed by 0.379 for exactly that reason.
python_cross_check.why_this_one_works: Every row of the Sobol design -- the A block, the B block and the hybrid blocks -- is a point whose coordinates are drawn from the input marginals, so the variance over all 8N evaluations estimates Var(f) regardless of how the rows are ordered. It checks the evaluations MOOSE actually produced against a closed form without depending on the design layout.
